sections.title: Playing
sections.info: How velocity becomes loudness, tone and attack. The graph shows the last key played: loudness (solid) and tone (dashed) across velocity, and a dot for each note you strike.

sections.title: Space
sections.info: The room around the piano. The measurements are close-miked, so Reverb 0 is the dry piano. Early reflections come from a model of each space; the tail is a smooth feedback network, so Decay, Size and Damping can be set freely.

accordion.title: Partial Arp
accordion.info: Not the arpeggiator below: this one plays inside each note. Each note's partials take their turn, a melody inside the note: by default each turn digs them out (Boost below 0 dB: a moving notch); a positive Boost brings them forward instead. Off leaves the piano as measured.

An arpeggiator and step sequencer that play piano notes from the keys you hold. Arp plays the held keys one after another; Sequencer lets each key sound and adds its own pattern of notes above it. Each note is a full piano strike, ended by its damper (Note Envelope Off, the default) or by the note envelope.

Routes from a source (an LFO, a Shape, velocity, the key, a random value per note, the mod wheel, the beat, the arpeggiator's envelopes…) to the piano's controls. Tone and hammer settings are read as each note is struck, so a route there gives each note its own tone; the strings' Sustain, Unison, Dampers and Overtone Decay and the Partial Arp follow it as notes ring; Space and the phrase envelope follow sources shared by all notes (Global LFOs, Shapes on Bar, Beat or Free, the wheel, the beat). Pitch and Level (vibrato, tremolo) move every note.

paramInfo.play.touch: How hard you have to play. Light: quiet playing already reaches the loud, bright end. Heavy: you need to dig in.
paramInfo.play.dynamics: The loudness range between the softest and hardest strike. 100% is the recorded piano's own range; lower keeps soft notes louder.
paramInfo.tone.bright: Tilts every note's partials: more or less treble per octave of overtones, like harder or softer hammers.
paramInfo.tone.hammer: The strike at the start of each note: the hammer, key and soundboard's own response, as recorded from A2 up (octave bands of noise below). 0 dB is as measured.
paramInfo.string.unison: How far the two or three strings of each note are out of tune with each other: the slow beating in a sustained note, and in the treble the spread of each partial's cluster. 100% is as measured; 0% is a perfectly tuned unison.
paramInfo.string.stretch: The recorded piano's stretch tuning: low notes flatter and high notes sharper, as a tuner sets a real piano to match its stiff strings. 0% is plain equal temperament.
paramInfo.string.sustain: How long notes ring. 100% is as measured.
paramInfo.string.damper: How long the dampers take to stop a note when you let go of the key. Keys above E6 have no dampers, as on a grand (Top Dampers changes that).
paramInfo.space.width: Stereo width of the two microphones the piano was measured with.
paramInfo.space.room: How much of the space you hear. The measurements are close-miked, so 0 is the dry piano.
paramInfo.tone.attack: How long each note takes to swell in at the strike. 100% is as measured for each key, from the recordings.
paramInfo.tone.body: The soundboard and room ringing on after each strike: the echo-like tail most audible on high notes. 0 dB is as measured. The key's damper stops it when you let go (above E6, where a grand has no dampers, it rings on unless Top Dampers is All keys).
paramInfo.play.tone: How much the tone darkens as you play softer. 100% is as recorded: each loudness has the tone the real piano had at that loudness. Lower keeps soft notes brighter; higher makes them darker and gentler.
paramInfo.play.softattack: How much softer notes swell in more slowly, as the hammer's felt stays on the string longer at gentle blows. 0% swells in at the measured speed whatever the velocity.
paramInfo.play.velmap: Smooth: velocity moves evenly through this piano's loudness range, with the tone that goes with each loudness. As Recorded: the sample library's own velocity layers, unevenly spaced as recorded.
paramInfo.tone.mech: The piano's mechanical sounds: each key's own noise as it comes back up and its damper lands, and the sustain pedal's thump going down and up. Measured from the recordings; 0 dB is the level the sample library mixes them at.
paramInfo.string.resonance: Sympathetic resonance: strings whose dampers are up (all of them with the sustain pedal down, and those above E6, which have none) pick up the notes you play and ring along, most where their overtones line up with the notes'. 0 dB is the default strength; −40 dB turns it off. Pressing the pedal sets the free strings ringing on its own; that follows Key & Pedal.
paramInfo.string.topdampers: A grand has no dampers above E6: those notes ring on after you let go, fading as they would held. All keys: every key is damped on release, as on many digital pianos.
paramInfo.tone.hardness: The hammer's felt. Softer dulls the partials and the strike and swells in more slowly, down to a felt-piano mute at -100%; harder brightens them and swells in faster. It moves the corner of the hammer's spectrum, measured per key and velocity from the recordings, up to three octaves either way. 0% is the recorded piano.
paramInfo.tone.strikepoint: Where along the string the hammer strikes, as a share of its length. Nearer the end (lower) is thinner and brighter; further in is darker and hollower, as the partials with a node there go quiet. The recorded piano strikes at about 12% (1/8).
paramInfo.string.stiffness: How stiff the strings are: their inharmonicity, which spreads the upper partials sharp of whole multiples of the fundamental. 0% is an ideal, harmonic string (harp-like, organ-like in the bass); 100% is the measured piano; above, stiffer, towards bells and gongs. It applies to the notes you strike next.
paramInfo.string.overtonedecay: How long the upper partials ring compared with the measured piano, the fundamental's decay kept. Below 0%, they ring on longer (bright, steely); above, they die sooner (dark, like gut or nylon strings).
paramInfo.parp.pattern: The order the partials take their turn: up the series, down, up and back, or at random (never the same twice running). Off turns the arpeggiator off: the piano as measured.
paramInfo.parp.scale: Which partials take part, by the pitch each harmonic has against the note: Major Pentatonic (harmonics 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 27…), Minor Pentatonic (with the 7th harmonic as the flat seventh), Major Triad, every harmonic, or the odd ones only (hollow, clarinet-like). The piano's stiff strings tune the upper partials a little sharp of these.
paramInfo.parp.low: The lowest partial in the pattern (1 is the fundamental). Partials below it, and above Highest, are left as they are.
paramInfo.parp.high: The highest partial in the pattern. High keys have fewer partials: the pattern uses only those the note has.
paramInfo.parp.rate: Steps per second, when Sync is off. Each note starts its pattern when it's struck.
paramInfo.parp.sync: Lock the step length to the tempo, at Division.
paramInfo.parp.division: The step length when Sync is on.
paramInfo.parp.overlap: How long each partial's swell lasts against the step. 100%: it takes two steps, so one partial rises while the last one falls. 0%: each has its step to itself, a pulse. 200%: three at once, a smear.
paramInfo.parp.boost: How far a featured partial moves at its turn, against its natural level. Negative (the default, -20 dB) digs it out: a moving notch, the more natural sound. Positive brings it forward instead, which stands out more but can sound resonant; try Octaves and some Width with it.
paramInfo.parp.others: Where the pattern's other partials sit while it's not their turn. 0 dB leaves them as measured; lower thins the note to the pattern, with the partials outside it (below Lowest, above Highest) carrying on as usual.
paramInfo.parp.group: Single: each step features one partial (sharp, whistle-like when boosted). Octaves: a step is a pitch of the scale, and every partial of it in range moves together (E: 5, 10 and 20), so the melody comes from across the spectrum rather than one sine.
paramInfo.parp.width: Spreads each featured partial to its neighbours within this many octaves either side, fading with distance: a moving formant rather than a single partial. 0: only the featured partials.
paramInfo.space.type: The space: Room (a small room, 0.6 s), Chamber (1.3 s), Hall (a concert hall, 2.2 s), Cathedral (5 s) or Plate (a bright, dense studio plate, 2.4 s, no reflections). Changing it lets the old space ring out.
paramInfo.space.decay: The tail's length against the space's own (its RT60). 100 % is the space as designed.
paramInfo.space.size: Scales the tail's delays: smaller is denser and more metallic, larger is grainier and more spacious. The decay time stays. Moving it while a tail rings bends its pitch a little, like a tape.
paramInfo.space.predelay: A gap before the reverb starts, on top of the space's own distances: a bigger stage, and a clearer attack.
paramInfo.space.damping: How much faster the treble dies than the rest. 50 % is the space's own; 0 % keeps the treble as long as the body (bright, glassy); 100 % makes it die quickly (warm, dark).
paramInfo.space.early: The early reflections' level against the tail: up for a sense of walls close by, down for a tail that blooms on its own.
paramInfo.space.lowcut: Takes the bass out of the reverb only, so low notes don't turn muddy.
paramInfo.space.highcut: Takes the top out of the reverb only, for a softer, more distant space.
